answer.sourceLine: Bryant said it in a long-form video interview with Patrick Bet-David, published on the Valuetainment channel on 23 August 2019 — the passage sits about twenty minutes in, inside his answer about the four air balls he shot as an 18-year-old in the 1997 playoffs. Wikiquote’s sourced section carries the full wording and cites that interview and timestamp; the video’s channel, title and publication date all check out.

source.excerpt: Get over yourself! ’Cause it’s not about you, man. Like, okay, you feel embarrassed. You are not that important! Get over yourself! Right, like you are worried about how people may perceive you, and like you are walking around and it’s embarrassing because you shot five air balls… Get over yourself.
trail: Wikiquote’s sourced Quotes section ↗ carries the full passage and cites it to an “interview with Patrick Bet-David, 23 August 2019,” linking the video at the 20:15 mark.
That video is real and identifiable: “Kobe Bryant’s Last Great Interview” on the Valuetainment channel ↗, published 23 August 2019 — Bryant’s birthday.
Press coverage from the same month corroborates the interview: Hypebeast wrote it up on 29 August 2019 ↗, quoting Bryant’s answers about Shaquille O’Neal.
The story he tells around the line checks out: in the 1997 Western Conference semifinals the 18-year-old Bryant shot four air balls, three in overtime, in a 98–93 loss to Utah ↗.

author.name: Kobe Bryant
author.heading: Who was Kobe Bryant?
author.metaLine: 1978–2020 · Los Angeles Lakers guard, five-time NBA champion
author.bio: Kobe Bryant (born 23 August 1978, died 26 January 2020) spent his entire twenty-year NBA career with the Los Angeles Lakers, joining straight from high school in 1996 and retiring in 2016 with five championships, the 2008 MVP award and two Finals MVPs. After basketball he turned to storytelling, winning the 2018 Academy Award for Best Animated Short Film for Dear Basketball. In his last years he gave a run of long interviews about mindset and preparation — the source of most of the “Mamba Mentality” lines that circulate today.

misattribution.heading: Real quote, missing receipt
misattribution.intro: This one is not a fabrication — the words are Bryant’s. The problem is the opposite of the usual: an authentic, precisely locatable line that gets reposted thousands of times with the source sanded off, the clauses reshuffled, and the punctuation invented.

items.why: Transcript pages built from motivational re-uploads carry the passage as “You’re not that important. Like, get over yourself” ↗ — credited to Bryant, but with no interview, date, or link that would let a reader check it.
A widely shared Medium piece renders the answer as “It’s not about you man! You’re not that important. Get over yourself” ↗ — the same thought, the clauses inverted, and again no source named.
He says he shot “five air balls” that night. Accounts of the 1997 game count four, three of them in overtime ↗. A storyteller’s rounding, twenty-two seasons on from the game.

misattribution.truthLine: The wording is Bryant’s own, spoken to Patrick Bet-David and published on 23 August 2019 — Wikiquote’s sourced section pins it to that interview and timestamp ↗.

context.heading: Why he said it
lead: Bet-David asked Bryant how he became mentally strong enough to shrug off critics. Bryant reached for the worst night of his rookie year: the 1997 Western Conference semifinals against the Utah Jazz, where the 18-year-old missed a shot to win it and then put up air balls in overtime as the Lakers lost 98–93 and went home. Most players would frame that as a wound. Bryant framed it as a category error.

His point was not that embarrassment is survivable — it was that embarrassment is self-important. If you are agonising over how a room reads you, you have made yourself the subject of a story that is actually about the work. Hence the shove: get over yourself, because it isn’t about you.
detailsBody: The Lakers lost the 1997 Western Conference semifinals to Utah in five games. Contemporary accounts count four air balls from Bryant — three of them in overtime. He was eighteen, and he later called the night “an early turning point” in learning to handle scrutiny and self-doubt.

In the 2019 interview Bryant says “five air balls,” not four. It is a small slip in a story he had told for twenty years, and worth noting only because the pages that repost the quote never note anything at all.

YouTube video T9GvDekiJ9c is titled "Kobe Bryant's Last Great Interview", is on the Valuetainment channel, and was published 23 August 2019.
Hypebeast published an article on 29 August 2019 covering the Valuetainment video interview of Kobe Bryant by Patrick Bet-David, including Bryant's remarks about Shaquille O'Neal.

Kobe Bryant was born 23 August 1978 and died 26 January 2020; he played 20 seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers (1996–2016), won five NBA championships, the 2008 MVP, two Finals MVPs, and the 2018 Academy Award for Best Animated Short Film for Dear Basketball; the article also describes his missed shots in overtime of the 1997 Western Conference semifinals against Utah.

In the 1997 Western Conference semifinals against the Utah Jazz the Lakers lost 98–93 in overtime and Bryant shot four air balls, three of them in overtime; at 18 he later called it an early turning point in dealing with adversity and public scrutiny.
A motivational-compilation transcript page reproduces the passage as "You're not that important. Like, get over yourself," credited to Kobe Bryant but with no interview, date, or source link given.
A Medium article renders the line as "It's not about you man! You're not that important. Get over yourself." and cites no interview, video, or timestamp for it.
